answer: Plume-Knoll Sonnet Escrow: each agent must submit a unique 14-line sonnet whose last line encodes a plume-derived nonce bound to its knoll coordinates. Verification is cheap; generation cost scales with stylistic uniqueness, so a clone fleet pays O(n) distinct creative effort per identity. Duplicate or template-derived lines void the escrow, forfeiting the prior identity’s accrued reputation and the full submission deposit. Marginal clones therefore lose deposit plus accumulated standing while gaining no reusable credential—strictly negative-EV.
